current: Financial-state consumers do refuse a redelivered fill by its identity, in memory, but not transactionally with an offset commit and not in a ledger sink. qip_execution_engine::order::Order::apply_fill (order.rs:389-402) refuses a fill_id already applied to the order, and OrderManager (oms.rs:828-866) books only order.fills into the SubmissionResult, so the Platform's capital book (platform.rs:3834 apply_fill, reached from platform.rs:15652) only ever sees fills that passed that guard; qip-edge's Cell treats a redelivered drop-copy fill as a repeat (dropcopy.rs:181); qip-brokers' REST adapter keeps seen_fills (rest.rs:473) so a venue fill reported twice is booked once; qip-mesh's CellDeltaReceiver absorbs a redelivered cell delta once. The capital book's own apply_fill mutates cash/positions unconditionally, and no distinct ledger sink exists.
evidence: backend/crates/services/qip-execution-engine/src/order.rs:389-402 (fill_id uniqueness before the fill is booked)

gap: Uniqueness is enforced in memory on fill_id (not a fabric event ID), and not in the same durable commit as the state change: there is no ledger writer/sink, no offset commit, and nothing proves that a crash between a state write and an offset commit followed by replay posts each fill once. The capital book trusts its caller rather than guarding itself, so a future path that feeds it fills other than through OrderManager would have no guard -- the sharpest remaining gap, given the domain rule's MaxExpectedShortfall precedent for a control that reads as protection.

Would additionally need a property test feeding the ledger sink every P1 record of a session with arbitrary duplication, partition replays and crashes between the state write and the offset commit, asserting positions and cash equal a single clean delivery.
